releases.title: Squads, new modes and real sights
releases.summary: Squads with revives, Team Deathmatch, Capture the Flag and Rush, sights modelled on real ones, a soundtrack, and far fewer frame drops.

entries.title: Squads and revives.
entries.text: You join a squad of four. Deploy on a squadmate, and see your squad in a panel and marked in green. Medics carry a defibrillator: stand over a fallen teammate to bring them back where they fell.

images.alt: First person behind two squadmates on The Depot, the defibrillator in the gadget list
images.caption: Back on their feet

entries.title: Three new game modes.
entries.text: Team Deathmatch, Capture the Flag (first to three captures) and Rush (attackers arm two objectives a stage, over three stages). Pick one in the match setup.

images.alt: Rush on The Depot: objective A armed, a fuse counting down
images.caption: Rush, objective A armed

entries.title: Real sights and new attachments.
entries.text: Every sight is now a real model: EOTech EXPS3, Aimpoint T-2, Trijicon RMR, Holosun HS510C, Spitfire 3x, ACOG TA31, Razor 1-6x, Mark 4 and PM II. New: the Aimpoint CompM4, the PSO-1 on the AK side rail with its rangefinder reticle, the Grip-Pod and an offset light. Bipods stand when you lie down or rest the gun, lights and lasers switch with L, and the D-60 drum is remodelled.

images.alt: Looking through a PSO-1 scope on an AK-74 at a target board, its chevrons and windage scale lit
images.caption: PSO-1 4x

entries.title: Far fewer frame drops.
entries.text: Soldiers are now animated on the graphics card: looking over the deployment with 64 soldiers went from about 30 to over 150 fps on an RTX 5060 laptop. A launch screen shows at once and the title is up in under two seconds.

entries.title: A new look.
entries.text: A new title screen with the version on it, a Colour setting (Natural, Rich, Vivid) with deeper shadows and fuller colour, and more effects: sparks and embers in explosions, dust and sparks where bullets hit, embers above fires, dust from slides and dives.

images.alt: The title screen: two soldiers at golden hour behind sandbags, the menu on the left
images.caption: The new title

entries.title: A soundtrack.
entries.text: A title theme, a deploy piece, a battle theme as the match starts, and victory and defeat themes. Music has its own volume slider.

entries.title: The official server in the browser.
entries.text: The web version has a Servers page, and the official server takes players from the browser and from the Windows and Linux versions alike.

entries.title: Neck shots.
entries.text: Bullets and rockets at neck height went through a soldier between the chest and the head. They hit now.

releases.title: Finer detail, and the launcher on servers
releases.summary: Soldiers near you, every attachment and the guns' round parts are drawn in finer detail, and the underbarrel grenade launcher now works for players on a server.

entries.title: The underbarrel launcher on servers.
entries.text: On a server, the official one included, B said there was no launcher under the gun even with an M203 or GP-25 fitted. It now brings the launcher up and its grenades fly, as they always did offline.

images.alt: First person holding an AK-74 with a GP-25, the launcher tag beside the ammo showing B and Rifle
images.caption: The GP-25 up, B back to the rifle

entries.title: Soldiers up close.
entries.text: Within about 16 m soldiers are drawn in finer detail: rounder limbs, boots, hands and helmets, pocket snaps, knee pad buckles, boot tread, a sleeve pocket with a flag patch, glove seams, webbing loops round the vest and belt, buckles, zips, a drag handle, and a light, strobe and shock cord on the helmet. Further off they keep the plain body, so a full fight costs about the same.

images.alt: A soldier's plate carrier, sleeves and belt up close, with buckles, webbing and a sleeve pocket
images.caption: The near body

entries.title: Attachments and guns.
entries.text: Clamp nuts and bolts, adjuster screws, lens rings, ring screws on scopes, flutes and vents on suppressors, notched bipod legs, a light's bezel and tail switch, lenses, knobs and a selector on laser boxes, the drum's winding key. Every gun's barrels, tubes, grips and knobs are smoother too.

images.alt: An M4A1 with a 1-6x scope, flash hider, stubby grip and light, side-on
images.caption: Scope rings, clamp and grip up close

entries.title: A slower first load.
entries.text: The first match after updating takes about 20 seconds to load while the new parts are shaded. After that it's as quick as before.

releases.title: Tighter maps and swimming
releases.summary: Every map closes in, with less open ground and more cover between the deployments. Deep water is swum, not walked, ammo types join Create a class, and the HUD shows the controller's buttons when you play on one.

entries.title: Tighter maps.
entries.text: The play area is about a sixth smaller across and the deployments sit closer. The open ground between them now has forward posts, huts, low walls, groves of trees and loose cover to move between.

images.alt: The Depot from above: the container yard, the depot buildings and the outposts, with cover and huts across the open ground
images.caption: The Depot, tighter

entries.title: Swimming.
entries.text: Deep water floats you with your eyes just above the surface. You swim slower than you walk, faster with sprint held, with the gun lowered. Walk out at a bank, or press Jump at a quay to climb out. Bots keep out of deep water and cross by the bridges.

images.alt: First person, swimming in Timberline's river with a wooden bridge ahead
images.caption: In Timberline's river

entries.title: Ammo types.
entries.text: A new slot in Create a class. Rifles, SMGs and pistols take standard, hollow point (harder up close, falls off sooner), armour piercing (goes through thin walls) or subsonic (slow, near silent under a suppressor). Shotguns take buckshot, slugs or flechettes.

entries.title: Controller prompts.
entries.text: With a controller in hand the HUD and loading tips show its buttons: LB and RB for gadgets, d-pad up for a killstreak, X to reload. On the keyboard they show your own key bindings.

images.alt: The match HUD with LB and RB beside the gadgets, a d-pad beside the killstreak and Press X to reload
images.caption: Playing on a controller

entries.title: Underbarrel launchers.
entries.text: B, or d-pad left on a controller, switches to the M203 or GP-25 and back. With no launcher fitted it now says so, and a tag beside the ammo shows the launcher, its rounds and its button.

releases.title: 32 a side
releases.summary: Every map grew for 64 soldiers: five flags across a wider front, an outpost on each flank and a long approach from each deployment. The M32 loads like the real one, and the Steam Deck's keyboard types into the game.

entries.title: Maps for 32 a side.
entries.text: Each map keeps its middle and its three flags and gains a ring round them: an outpost with a flag on each flank, deployments further back, and between them cover lines, forward posts and a belt of trees that hides each spawn.

images.alt: The Depot from high above: both deployments, the middle and the outposts on the flanks
images.caption: The Depot for 32 a side

images.alt: First person at the deployment with five flags A to E across the top of the screen
images.caption: Five flags

entries.title: Flank outposts.
entries.text: A logging camp and a radio relay at the Depot, a mud-house hamlet and a checkpoint at Sandstone, a radar site and a hangar yard at Redwing, a farmstead and a checkpoint in Old Town, bridges over Timberline's river, dockside depots at Port Anvil.

images.alt: A wooden bridge over Timberline's river with cabins on the banks
images.caption: Timberline's new crossing

images.alt: A logging camp with cabins, stacked logs and a truck
images.caption: The Depot's logging camp

entries.title: 32 bots a side.
entries.text: Bots go up to 32 a side (16 by default) and tickets up to 1200. Dedicated servers run 32 a side by default, the official server too.

entries.title: The M32 reloads like the real one.
entries.text: The frame swings open to the side, each grenade goes into the chamber beside the barrel and the cylinder winds round to the next. Its red dot sight is no longer blocked.

images.alt: The M32's open cylinder with four chambers loaded
images.caption: Loading the M32

entries.title: Typing on the Steam Deck.
entries.text: The on-screen keyboard now types into the server address and sign-in boxes, and opens by itself when you pick one. Enter joins from the address box.

releases.title: Accounts, a server list and an official server
releases.summary: Make a Frontface account and your name follows you onto every scoreboard. Servers now list themselves on a new page of the title screen, and an official server is up in the US East.

entries.title: Accounts.
entries.text: Sign in or make an account from the top right of the title screen, or on the accounts page at 129-80-83-173.sslip.io. Without one you play as Guest and a number.

images.alt: The title screen's account panel with name and password boxes
images.caption: Sign in from the title screen

entries.title: Server list.
entries.text: Servers on the title screen lists every running dedicated server with its map and players, and joins in one click. Dedicated servers list themselves; a hosted game can be listed from the match setup.

images.alt: The Servers page listing Frontface official (US East) on The Depot
images.caption: The server list

entries.title: Official server.
entries.text: Frontface official (US East) runs all six maps around the clock for signed-in players.

entries.title: Aim over cover.
entries.text: Raise your gun over a wall or ledge in front of you to aim and fire over it.

entries.title: Underbarrel launchers, Kobra and reticles.
entries.text: The M203 and GP-25 sit flush under the barrel with their own trigger, round and leaf sight. A side-mounted Kobra for the AK-74, RPK and SVD, and a choice of reticle saved with each class.

entries.title: Launchers.
entries.text: Rockets and grenades fly with real speeds and drop, and blasts are bigger.

entries.title: Bots.
entries.text: Bots move as squads, clear rooms and go for the flags first.

entries.title: The scoreboard fits a full server.
entries.text: Rows shrink to fit both sides, and past about 30 a side the board scrolls with the mouse wheel, starting at your own row.

images.alt: The scoreboard with twenty players on each side
images.caption: Twenty a side

entries.title: Names online.
entries.text: Every player used to be called You on a server. Now it's your account name, or a Guest name.

releases.label: Launchers
releases.title: Launchers for Windows and Steam Deck
releases.summary: Frontface now installs and updates through its own launcher on Windows and on the Steam Deck, with builds from GitHub. The browser version went live the same day, and servers can take browser players.

entries.title: Frontface Launcher.
entries.text: Install, update and play Windows builds, keep older versions side by side, join a server by its address, and read these notes.

entries.title: Steam Deck launcher.
entries.text: A Linux launcher for the Deck that works with the controller in Game Mode, opens Steam's keyboard for the Join box, and updates itself.

entries.title: Native Linux build.
entries.text: From 0.1.1 every version also comes for Linux, so the Deck runs Frontface without Proton. Windows and Deck players can join each other's servers.

entries.title: Play in the browser.
entries.text: frontface-neon.vercel.app runs the game against bots in Chrome with WebGPU, no install.

entries.title: Servers for browser players.
entries.text: A dedicated server can speak WebSockets (websocket = 1 in server.cfg), so browser and desktop players can play on the same server.

entries.title: Controller support.
entries.text: Move, aim, lean while aiming, throw gadgets and work the menus with a gamepad.

entries.title: Steady aim.
entries.text: Hold sprint while scoped to hold your breath against the sway.

entries.title: Stims for every class.
entries.text: Every class can carry a stim shot.

entries.title: 12 more guns.
entries.text: More guns for every class.

entries.title: Every launcher for Support.
entries.text: Support can now carry all of the launchers.

entries.title: Display and Resolution settings.
entries.text: Choose full screen or windowed and a resolution under Settings, Graphics.

entries.title: Black bars under Proton.
entries.text: Full screen at the wrong shape snaps back to the monitor's size, and the Resolution list uses that real size (0.1.1 and 0.1.2).

releases.label: Arsenal
releases.title: Thirty-three guns, launchers and a dedicated server
releases.summary: Every gun rebuilt from real photographs, a gun list per class, launchers, new ways to move, new maps and a server you can run at home.

entries.title: 33 guns, each owned by a class.
entries.text: Assault, Support, Medic, Recon and Breacher each have their own guns; pistols go with any class. Lengths are within a few millimetres of the real ones.

images.alt: Six guns side by side
images.caption: Measured from photographs

entries.title: Launchers.
entries.text: LAW, Carl Gustaf, RPG-7 and M32, plus M203 and GP-25 grenade launchers under the rifle.

images.alt: An RPG-7 round going off
images.caption: RPG-7

entries.title: Two gadget slots and killstreaks.
entries.text: Each class picks two gadgets, and a run of kills earns more.

entries.title: Optics that really magnify.
entries.text: A 4x scope shows 4x, measured on a target at 60 m. Canted sights for close range.

images.alt: Looking through a 4x ACOG
images.caption: 4x ACOG

entries.title: New ways to move.
entries.text: Prone, dive to prone, crouch slide, vault over cover and through windows, mount your gun on cover while aiming, and a tactical sprint (double-tap Shift).

entries.title: Redwing Airfield and Old Town.
entries.text: Two new maps, and The Depot redone as a mirrored map so neither side starts ahead.

images.alt: Redwing Airfield from above
images.caption: Redwing Airfield

images.alt: Old Town from above
images.caption: Old Town

entries.title: Dedicated server.
entries.text: A Windows server package with server.cfg and a map rotation that keeps players between matches.

entries.title: A voice for every soldier.
entries.text: Each soldier keeps one voice for all of their lines.

entries.title: Guns rebuilt.
entries.text: Low poly but detailed: real cuts, rounded grips, pins, knurling and roll marks, with smoother reloads.

entries.title: Hands sit on the gun.
entries.text: Both hands reach the grip, handguard and charging handle in first and third person, through every reload.

entries.title: Smoke, fire and light.
entries.text: Soft lit smoke, flame, light shafts and indoor exposure.

images.alt: A smoke grenade going off
images.caption: Smoke

images.alt: Light shafts in Old Town
images.caption: Light shafts

entries.title: Graphics options.
entries.text: Anti-aliasing, shadows, ambient occlusion, depth of field, bloom, motion blur, grain, light shafts, render scale and a frame cap.

entries.title: Bots.
entries.text: Bots notice you gradually and fight at the range their gun suits.

entries.title: Shots stopped by invisible walls.
entries.text: Bullets now hit the shape of the cover you see, not a box around it.

releases.label: First playable
releases.title: Frontface is playable
releases.summary: Conquest against bots or friends, real guns with real reloads, your own classes and four maps.

entries.title: Conquest.
entries.text: Take and hold the flags; the side that runs out of tickets loses.

images.alt: Spawning on The Depot
images.caption: The Depot

entries.title: Six real guns.
entries.text: M4A1, AK-74, MP5A3, Glock 17, Model 870 and M24, with magazine reloads and spent brass.

entries.title: Online play.
entries.text: Host a game or join one by address.

entries.title: Create a class.
entries.text: Five saved classes, attachments for every gun, and gadgets for each role.

images.alt: The create-a-class screen
images.caption: Create a class

entries.title: Four maps.
entries.text: The Depot, Sandstone, Port Anvil and Timberline.

entries.text: Title screen, loading, deploy, pause, settings, death and end-of-match screens.

entries.title: Props from the 3D studio.
entries.text: Seventeen props, from the APC to the satellite dish, made in the AI 3D studio and drawn in the game's own style.

images.caption: Studio props in a match

inProgress.title: A real Steam Deck
inProgress.body: The Deck launcher and the Linux build were tested on Linux on a PC: installing, and joining a server from the launcher. Running them on a Deck, with the game drawn on the Deck's own GPU, comes next.

inProgress.title: Browser players on the official server
inProgress.body: The official server is up for Windows and Deck players. Browser players need it to speak secure WebSockets (wss://) as well, which comes next.

inProgress.title: Real controllers
inProgress.body: Controller support was built and tested with scripted input; it still needs a real gamepad in hand.

inProgress.title: Playing by hand
inProgress.body: Every build is checked by scripts. Long matches with a real mouse, LAN games and listening to the new sounds come next.
